findings.quote: neither block needs to push on the other to keep pace
findings.note: 'keep pace' is an idiom, and 'needs to push' gives the block a wish; the brief asks for literal textbook English. The physics of the line is correct.
findings.fix: Since both blocks would accelerate at the same rate even if they were separate, no contact force is needed for them to move together.

notes: Independent solve: on a smooth incline each block alone has a = g sin30 regardless of mass, so the two move together with zero contact force. Final answer and every equation agree with mine. common_mistakes[1]'s number 10 N reproduces from (4 - 2) g sin30 with g = 10. 'From rest' is not needed by the solution and not needed by the physics.
